question: Which of the following antitussive can lead to hallucinations
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Dextromethorphan" -> "NMDA receptor antagonist" -> "increased risk of dissociative effects" -> "possible hallucinations" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Diphenhydramine" -> "anticholinergic properties" -> "CNS effects including confusion" -> "possible hallucinations" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Morphine" -> "opioid receptor agonist" -> "CNS depression" -> "possible altered mental status" -> "possible hallucinations" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Aprepitant" -> "substance P/neurokinin 1 receptor antagonist" -> "not commonly associated with hallucinations" -> "unlikely to cause hallucinations" -> 20%
analysis: Dextromethorphan is known to cause hallucinations, especially when taken in high doses. It acts on the NMDA receptor and can lead to dissociative effects similar to those of certain hallucinogens. Morphine and diphenhydramine can have sedative effects, but they are not primarily associated with hallucinations. Aprepitant is an antiemetic and does not typically cause hallucinations.
